name: NHTSA EMD National Standard Curriculum — EMDPRS elements

authority.instrument: Emergency Medical Dispatch: National Standard Curriculum (NHTSA, DOT HS 808 559)

provenance.source: NHTSA Emergency Medical Dispatch National Standard Curriculum, Instructor Guide + Trainee Guide (ERIC ED425308)
provenance.notes: US federal government work, public domain. The curriculum describes what an EMDPRS must contain — three protocol types, four design components per chief-complaint card, the initial-survey contents, and the 32 chief complaint types — but deliberately ships no filled-in cards; the sample pages are marked 'not approved for use'. Requirement wording here is condensed from the curriculum's own section headings, each cited to its module and unit.

chief-complaints-32.name: NHTSA 32 chief complaint types
chief-complaints-32.citation: Module 3, IG Note #1 — 'Present the Chief Complaints in the Following Order'; 11 traumatic incident types, 14 medical chief complaint types, 7 time/life-critical events

high-priority-symptoms.name: high-priority symptoms named by the curriculum
high-priority-symptoms.citation: Module 3, Unit 2 — 'The most common high-priority symptoms included in the majority of EMDPRS are chest pain, breathing problems, altered levels of consciousness and, in some cases, severe hemorrhage.'

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 1 — Descriptions of Three Protocol Types (1)
requirements.text: An Initial Survey / All-Caller Interrogation protocol: the questions asked of every caller, used to gather location (including telephone number) and patient status, and to point the EMD at the proper chief-complaint card.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 1 — Descriptions of Three Protocol Types (2)
requirements.text: Individual 'chief complaint' protocols, used to establish the type and severity of the emergency being reported and to verify what the all-caller interrogation gathered.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 1 — Descriptions of Three Protocol Types (3)
requirements.text: Scripted medical protocols: telephone instructions in script format, read to the caller word-for-word (the curriculum's examples are CPR, choking, childbirth, airway management).
requirements.notes: Checked as: at least one protocol carries an ordered instruction sequence of four or more steps.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 1 — four major design components (a)
requirements.text: Key Questions / Inquire of Caller: the additional, specific questions that gather the medical information the initial survey did not.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 1 — four major design components (b)
requirements.text: Dispatch Priorities (Medical Dispatch Criteria): the response allocations appropriate to the situation, dispatchable from the Key Questions alone.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 1 — four major design components (c)
requirements.text: Pre-Arrival Instructions: what to tell callers to prepare them and the patient for the arrival of the responders.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 1 — four major design components (d)
requirements.text: Useful Information: background, insights and possible complications for the EMD — explicitly not shared with the caller.
requirements.notes: Reported as unrepresentable until schema v0.3, which added protocols[].dispatcherNotes for exactly this — the cards' Call Taker Prompts, Dispatcher Short Report and Useful Information. Those string ids are kept disjoint from every spoken id, so the section stays EMD-facing by construction.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 1; Module 2, Unit 1 — 'Where?'
requirements.text: The initial survey gathers and verifies the incident location, even when E9-1-1/CAD supplies it.

requirements.citation: Module 2, Unit 1 — 'Get the phone number (aka call-back number)'
requirements.text: The initial survey gathers a call-back number, so contact can be re-established if the call drops.

requirements.citation: Module 2, Unit 1 — 'What?'; Module 3, Unit 2 — the survey directs the EMD to the proper card
requirements.text: The initial survey establishes the chief complaint, and the answer selects the chief-complaint protocol.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 1 — initial survey patient status; Module 3, Unit 2
requirements.text: The initial survey gathers the patient's age.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 1 — initial survey patient status
requirements.text: The initial survey gathers the patient's level of consciousness.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 1 — initial survey patient status
requirements.text: The initial survey gathers the patient's breathing status.

requirements.citation: Module 2, Unit 1 — 'The proper order that information should be gathered is Where, What, How, Who and When. This order is very important.'
requirements.text: Location is asked before the nature of the problem, so that some help can be sent if contact is lost.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 2 — 'If the patient is unconscious and not breathing … turn immediately to the appropriate protocol for the provision of CPR.'
requirements.text: The initial survey routes an unconscious, non-breathing patient straight to the cardiac-arrest/CPR protocol.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 2 — 6.1.2 'Describe the role of the EMD in providing telephone CPR'
requirements.text: The pack can deliver telephone CPR: patient positioning, hand placement, and compressions.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 2 — 'If the patient has merely choked and is not in cardiac arrest, you need to provide the instructions for choking intervention rather than CPR.'
requirements.text: Choking is handled by its own instruction path, distinct from CPR.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 2 — 4.1 'Identify the thirty-two chief complaint types'
requirements.text: The protocol set covers the thirty-two chief complaint types (11 traumatic, 14 medical, 7 time/life-critical).
requirements.notes: The curriculum itself notes that agencies group these differently — 'some have more while others may have less and … it is a locally decided issue'. Partial coverage is a scope statement, not a defect.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 2 — the most common high-priority symptoms
requirements.text: The protocol set covers the high-priority symptoms the curriculum names: chest pain, breathing problems, altered level of consciousness, and severe hemorrhage.

requirements.citation: Module 3, Unit 1 — 'the cards you use back at your site must be approved by the medical director of your EMS system'
requirements.text: The EMDPRS in use is approved by the EMS system's medical director.

check.note: a property of the agency that adopts a pack, not of the pack

requirements.citation: Course Description — 24-hour minimum course; Module 4 — Final Examination
requirements.text: Dispatchers complete the 24-hour minimum EMD course and its examination before using the EMDPRS.
